land.text: Dahala mandala (Baghelkhand), the Chedi country, with the capital Tripuri near Jabalpur

predecessors.note: Infobox: preceded by the Gurjara-Pratiharas. Under Kokalla I (850-890) the Kalachuris "were subordinate to the Pratihara emperor Bhoja". The page lists earlier chiefs from Vamaraja-deva (675-700) without territory, so the state is drawn from Kokalla I, "the first powerful ruler".

successors.note: Page: in the later 13th century former territories passed to "the Paramaras, Chandelas, the Delhi Sultanate and the Seunas (Yadavas of Devagiri)"; it does not say which part went to whom.
Same sentence (the Seunas); split not given.

capitals.name: Tripuri (Tewar, near Jabalpur)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Tripuri, "present-day Tewar near Jabalpur"; al-Biruni names the capital "Tiauri" (Gangeyadeva page). Coordinates are approximate (researcher's).

rulers.name: Gangeya-deva
rulers.note: infobox of the Gangeyadeva page: c. 1015 to 22 January 1041

rulers.name: Trailokya-malla
rulers.note: "c. 1210 - at least 1212"; the page says "It is not known when and how his rule ended."

correction.text: Dahala mandala (Baghelkhand), the Chedi country, with the capital Tripuri near Jabalpur

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kalachuri row). The infobox gives the realm as "Dahala mandala (Baghelkhand)", the capital Tripuri near Jabalpur, and no area. Kokalla I "appears to have laid the foundation of Kalachuri empire" (850-890). The two radii (Jabalpur 120 km, Rewa area 100 km) are the researcher's reading of Dahala.

union.text: Dahala mandala (Baghelkhand), the Chedi country, with the capital Tripuri near Jabalpur
the sacred cities of Varanasi and Prayaga

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Gangeyadeva "ultimately extended his control over the sacred cities of Varanasi and Prayaga"; the Ghaznavid raid on Varanasi in 1033 found it "under the rule of Ganga". Lakshmikarna's eastern raids (Anga, Vanga, Gauda) and his Malwa gains were not held and are not drawn; the Lakshmikarna page gives no extent. The Lata country, shown as Kalachuri in the Paramara and Chaulukya dossiers for 1056-1074, is on none of the pages opened here.

correction.text: Dahala mandala (Baghelkhand), the Chedi country, with the capital Tripuri near Jabalpur

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Yashahkarna "lost the northern parts of his kingdom, including Varanasi, to the Gahadavalas" (undated; 1085 is the year of Cliopatria's first Gahadavala shape). The Ratnapura branch under Kalingaraja since c. 1000 is a vassal, not drawn here.

New keyframe. Gayakarna "lost some of his northern territory to the Chandela king Madanavarman" and the Chandelas "captured the northern part of Baghelkhand"; the page gives no year (reign c. 1123-1153). The Ratnapura branch went independent under Ratna-deva II. Last ruler attested "at least until 1212".

region.text: Dahala mandala (Baghelkhand), the Chedi country, with the capital Tripuri near Jabalpur

ledger.note: 850: Kokalla I lays the foundation of the Kalachuri power at Tripuri. The page says he "appears to have laid the foundation of Kalachuri empire", dates his reign 850-890 and says the Kalachuris "were subordinate to the Pratihara emperor Bhoja". Reign dates are the page's list; the dynasty itself "ruled Dahala mandala (Baghelkhand) during 7th to 13th centuries".

region.text: Dakshina Kosala (Chhattisgarh), Kalinga-raja's Tummana near Bilaspur

ledger.note: c. 1000: the Ratnapura branch is set up in Chhattisgarh as a Tripuri vassal. "The Ratnapura branch was established by Kalinga-raja around 1000 CE ... They were an offshoot of the Kalachuris of Tripuri, and ruled as vassals of the parent dynasty for many years." Kalinga-raja took Dakshina Kosala from the Somavamshis and made Tummana his capital.

region.text: the sacred cities of Varanasi and Prayaga

ledger.note: 1033: Varanasi is Kalachuri. The Ghaznavid general Ahmad Niyaltigin raided Varanasi in 1033, when "the city was under the rule of Ganga"; the Pala-ruled city is attested "at least until 1016 CE" (Sarnath inscription of Mahipala). The page dates the attestation, not the conquest.

ledger.counterpart: unknown (page silent on who held Prayaga)
ledger.note: 1033 (bridge): Prayaga is added with Varanasi. "he ultimately extended his control over the sacred cities of Varanasi and Prayaga"; the page gives no year and no previous holder for Prayaga.

region.text: the Chandela kingdom of Devavarman around Khajuraho

ledger.note: c. 1050 (bridge): Lakshmikarna subjugates the Chandela Devavarman. "Lakshmikarna subjugated the Chandela king Devavarman (r. c. 1050-1060 CE)"; the Kalachuris page adds that Devavarman "seems to have died in a battle against him". The page gives no year for the subjugation; 1050 is the start of Devavarman's reign.

region.text: Around 1055 CE, he played an important role in the downfall of the Paramara king Bhoja

ledger.note: c. 1055: Lakshmikarna joins Bhima of Gujarat in the attack that topples the Paramara Bhoja. "Around 1055 CE, he played an important role in the downfall of the Paramara king Bhoja"; he "captured a part of the Paramara kingdom of Malwa after Bhoja's death" but lost it within months when "Jayasimha gained back his ancestral throne in 1055 CE"; later Lakshmikarna and Someshvara II took Malwa again, undated.

c. 1073: the Paramara Udayaditya ends the Kalachuri hold on Malwa. The Lakshmikarna page lists losing Malwa to Udayaditya "around 1073 CE" among the signs of decline, with the abdication to Yashahkarna.
1073: Yashahkarna raids Vengi. "This likely refers to Yashahkarna's raid on the Vengi Chalukya kingdom in 1073 CE, during the reign of Vijayaditya VII."
1073: the page gives the raid only; no withdrawal date.
before 1075-76: Kirttivarman frees the Chandela kingdom. Lakshmikarna "was ultimately ousted by Kirttivarman, sometime before 1075-76 CE".

union.text: the sacred cities of Varanasi and Prayaga

region.text: the northern parts of his kingdom, including Varanasi

ledger.note: 1085 (bridge): Varanasi and the north pass to the Gahadavalas. "Yashahkarna lost the northern parts of his kingdom, including Varanasi, to the Gahadavalas." The page gives no year; 1085 is the year of Cliopatria's first Gahadavala shape. The page does not name Prayaga here.

1123-1135 (bridge): Ratna-deva II of Ratnapura declares independence. "Ratna-deva II officially declared independence from the Kalachuris of Tripuri"; the Gayakarna page says it happened "during Gayakarna's reign" (c. 1123-1153) and that Gayakarna's army sent to subdue him "was defeated". Ratna-deva II reigns 1120-1135 on the Ratnapura list; 1123 is Gayakarna's accession.

c. 1152 (bridge): the Chandela Madanavarman takes northern Baghelkhand. "lost some of his northern territory to the Chandela king Madanavarman"; the Chandelas "captured the northern part of Baghelkhand". The page gives no year; 1152 is the year the Chandela dossier carries for the same event (Cliopatria's Chandela shape change).

c. 1212: last attested Kalachuri king. Trailokya-malla "ruled at least until 1212 CE"; "It is not known when and how his rule ended"; in the later 13th century the former territories passed to "the Paramaras, Chandelas, the Delhi Sultanate and the Seunas".

wars.name: Paramara raid on Tripuri
wars.outcome: Munja "invaded the Kalachuri kingdom and raided their capital Tripuri" in the reign of Yuvarajadeva II; no land is said to change hands.

wars.name: Gangeyadeva's campaigns

zones.text: the sacred cities of Varanasi and Prayaga

wars.outcome: Gangeyadeva fought the Kalyani Chalukyas, a Chandela (Vijayapala) and the Somavamshi Yayati without decisive result, took Varanasi (Pala-ruled until at least 1016) and Prayaga, and saw Ahmad Niyaltigin raid Varanasi in 1033, plundering it until noon before retreating.
wars.note: Western Chalukya of Kalyani is the page's "Chalukyas of Kalyani". Wars undated except the 1033 raid.

wars.name: Lakshmikarna's eastern campaigns
wars.outcome: The 1048-49 Rewa inscription claims successes in Anga and Vanga; the invasion of Gauda "was repulsed by Nayapala"; no land held; peace later sealed by the marriage of Yuvanashri to the Pala king.
wars.note: Undated except the 1048-49 inscription; the page is silent on Magadha, Utkala, Kosala and Lata.

wars.name: Fall of Bhoja and the war for Malwa
wars.outcome: Lakshmikarna and Bhima of Gujarat attacked Malwa about 1055 and Bhoja fell; Jayasimha regained the throne in 1055 with help from Vikramaditya VI; Lakshmikarna and Someshvara II took Malwa again until Udayaditya drove them out about 1073.

wars.name: Kalachuri-Chandela wars
wars.outcome: Vijayapala "broke the pride of Gangeyadeva in a battle"; Lakshmikarna subjugated Devavarman and was ousted by Kirttivarman before 1075-76; Madanavarman "captured the northern part of Baghelkhand" from Gayakarna.
wars.note: Years are the page reigns; the Chandela fights themselves are undated on all four pages.

wars.name: Ratnapura independence
wars.outcome: Ratna-deva II declared independence; Gayakarna's army "was defeated".

certainty.note: No treaty line on any page opened; Dahala (Baghelkhand and the Jabalpur country) is the stable core, every other limit is approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kalachuri row. Six pages. The Kalachuris of Tripuri page gives no founding or end year (rulers list from Vamaraja-deva 675-700; Kokalla I 850-890 'appears to have laid the foundation'), so the state is drawn 850-1212 with the end 'at least until 1212'. Gaps that need another page: the Lata country (southern Gujarat) is shown as Kalachuri 1056-1074 in the paramara-dynasty and chaulukya-dynasty dossiers but is not on any page opened here; the Kalinjar loss to the Chandelas before 954 and the eastern parts lost to Gangeya c. 1035 are in the chandela-kingdom dossier; Karna's Magadha and Gauda gains are not on the pages. Years marked 'bridge' are the researcher's, matched to the neighbours' dossiers (Gahadavala 1085, Chandela 1152). Gazetteer names wanted: Baghelkhand / Dahala, Tripuri (Tewar), Rewa, Kalinjar. The Ratnapura branch now has its own dossier in this batch (kalachuris-of-ratnapura; sa-03-g refers to it as kalachuri-of-ratnapura), as does the Somavamshi dynasty (somavamshi-dynasty).
